original_question: Let f be a geometrically finite rational map, meaning that its post-critical set P meets its Julia set J in only finitely many points, equivalently every critical point in J is preperiodic. Must one have either J equal to the whole sphere with the action of f on J ergodic, or else Hausdorff dimension delta(J) < 2? In the latter case, what can be said about the delta-dimensional measure of J and the dynamics relative to that measure class?
target_in_paper: C. McMullen, "Geometrically finite maps and Kleinian groups," subsection "Geometrically finite rational maps," Problem 1 in arXiv:math/9201271 (Conformal dynamics problem list).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact formulation. It correctly identifies the hypothesis of geometric finiteness, includes the equivalent condition that every critical point in the Julia set is preperiodic, states the intended dichotomy between the full-sphere case and the Hausdorff-dimension-<2 case, and preserves the paper's follow-up question about the delta-dimensional measure and the dynamics relative to that measure class. In substance, it is essentially Problem 1 paraphrased.
missing_details: The map should be stated as a rational self-map of the Riemann sphere (equivalently P^1(C)); this ambient space is implicit in the draft.
It is standard here that f has degree at least 2; that restriction is implicit rather than stated in the draft.

The nearby context defines C as the set of critical points of f, P as the post-critical set P = union over n >= 1 of f^n(C), and J as the Julia set; these definitions are needed for a fully stand-alone question.
The paper's notation is delta = dim_H(J), the Hausdorff dimension of J; writing delta(J) is understandable but not the paper's own notation.

The exact geometric-finiteness hypothesis in the paper is P intersect J is finite; the equivalent preperiodicity formulation should be explicitly tied to that definition, not just mentioned informally.
The dichotomy should be stated exactly as: either J is the whole sphere and the action of f on J is ergodic, or dim_H(J) < 2.

The phrase 'the action of f on J is ergodic' leaves the underlying measure implicit; the brief paper statement does not spell it out, so a stand-alone reformulation should acknowledge that this is an implicit part of the problem's meaning.
The phrase 'delta-dimensional measure of J' should be made explicit as the delta-dimensional Hausdorff measure, or at least as the Hausdorff-measure class in dimension delta.
The phrase 'the dynamics relative to that measure class' should be tied explicitly to the action of f on J with respect to that Hausdorff-measure class.
refined_question: Let f: P^1(C) -> P^1(C) be a rational map of degree at least 2, let C be its set of critical points, let P = union_{n>=1} f^n(C) be its post-critical set, and let J = J(f) be its Julia set. Assume f is geometrically finite in the sense that P intersect J is finite (equivalently, every critical point of f that lies in J is preperiodic). Must one have the following dichotomy: either J = P^1(C) and the action of f on J is ergodic, or else delta := dim_H(J) < 2? In the latter case, what can be said about the delta-dimensional Hausdorff measure of J and about the dynamics of f with respect to that measure class?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalent hypothesis only: Let f: P^1(C) -> P^1(C) be a rational map of degree at least 2 such that every critical point of f lying in the Julia set J(f) is preperiodic. Must either J(f) = P^1(C) with f|_{J(f)} ergodic, or dim_H(J(f)) < 2; and in the latter case, what can be said about the dim_H(J(f))-dimensional Hausdorff measure of J(f) and the dynamics with respect to that measure class?
justification: The draft matches McMullen's Problem 1 almost verbatim. In the immediately preceding lines, McMullen defines the post-critical set P and Julia set J, then says that a rational map is geometrically finite when P intersect J is finite, explicitly adding the equivalent formulation that every critical point in the Julia set is pre-periodic. Problem 1 then asks exactly for the dichotomy between the full-sphere ergodic case and the dim_H(J) < 2 case, followed by the question about the delta-dimensional measure of J and the corresponding dynamics. Because this arXiv item is a problem list, the closest official formulation is this Problem 1 itself, not a broader neighboring conjecture.
